title: Netherlands – Bicycles – EA Bedrijfsfietsen en handhavingsfietsen Gemeente Zwolle
description: De gemeente Zwolle sluit voor deze opdracht per perceel een Raamovereenkomst met één Opdrachtnemer. De Raamovereenkomsten hebben betrekking op de levering van fietsen in eigendom van de gemeente en het bijbehorende onderhoud, reparatie en service. Lease- en huurconstructies maken geen onderdeel uit van deze aanbesteding. De aanbesteding bestaat uit twee afzonderlijk te gunnen percelen: Perceel 1 – Handhavingsfietsen Dit perceel betreft de levering van handhavingsfietsen, waaronder robuuste fietsen zoals mountainbikes en elektrische varianten, die worden ingezet bij de uitvoering van toezicht- en handhavingstaken. Perceel 2 – Bedrijfsfietsen Dit perceel betreft de levering van elektrische en niet-elektrische bedrijfsfietsen. Deze fietsen worden ingezet als functioneel vervoermiddel ter ondersteuning van de dagelijkse werkzaamheden, met name voor korte dienstreizen en verplaatsingen tussen locaties. Omvang Perceel 1 – Handhavingsfietsen De geraamde opdrachtwaarde bedraagt € 156.392, - exclusief btw over de maximale looptijd van vier jaar. Om beperkte volumewijzigingen gedurende de looptijd te kunnen opvangen, wordt voor de reguliere scope een maximale opdrachtwaarde van € 195.490, - exclusief btw gehanteerd. Daarnaast is de volgende herzieningsmogelijkheid voorzien: Uitbreiding handhavingsfietsen: als gevolg van personele wijzigingen, veranderingen in mobiliteitsbeleid of organisatorische verschuivingen kan sprake zijn van uitbreiding met maximaal tien (10) handhavingsfietsen. De maximale financiële omvang van deze uitbreiding bedraagt € 56.000, - exclusief btw, bestaande uit maximaal € 50.000, - voor aanschaf en € 6.000, - voor onderdelen en onderhoud. Daarmee bedraagt de maximale financiële omvang voor Perceel 1 inclusief deze herzieningsmogelijkheid € 251.490, - exclusief btw. Omvang Perceel 2 – Bedrijfsfietsen De geraamde opdrachtwaarde bedraagt € 292.916, - exclusief btw over de maximale looptijd van vier jaar. Om beperkte volumewijzigingen gedurende de looptijd te kunnen opvangen, wordt voor de reguliere scope een maximale opdrachtwaarde van € 366.145, - exclusief btw gehanteerd. Daarnaast zijn de volgende herzieningsmogelijkheden voorzien: Uitbreiding elektrische bedrijfsfietsen: bij vervanging van reguliere bedrijfsfietsen kan gedurende de looptijd worden gekozen voor uitbreiding met maximaal vijftien (15) elektrische bedrijfsfietsen. De maximale financiële omvang hiervan bedraagt € 67.200, - exclusief btw, bestaande uit maximaal € 36.000, - voor aanschaf en € 31.200, - voor onderdelen en onderhoud. Uitbreiding elektrische bedrijfsfietsen in verband met dienstreizen: als gevolg van gewijzigd mobiliteitsbeleid kan voor een groep medewerkers behoefte ontstaan aan aanvullende elektrische fietsen. Hiervoor kan de vloot worden uitgebreid met maximaal twintig (20) elektrische bedrijfsfietsen. De maximale financiële omvang van deze uitbreiding bedraagt € 104.000, - exclusief btw. Daarmee bedraagt de maximale financiële omvang voor Perceel 2 inclusief deze herzieningsmogelijkheden € 537.345, - exclusief btw. De totale maximale financiële omvang van beide percelen gezamenlijk bedraagt daarmee € 788.835, - exclusief btw. De betreffende Raamovereenkomst eindigt uiterlijk na afloop van de maximale contractduur of eerder wanneer de voor het betreffende perceel geldende maximale opdrachtwaarde is bereikt.

title: Germany – Demolition work – VE8309HB - Rückbau im Bereich des VKN München
description: Gegenstand der Maßnahme ist der Schadstoffsanierung, Entkernung und Abbruch im Bereich des Verkehrsknotenpunktes (VKN) Hbf München. Für die Herstellung der Vorhaltemaßnahme U9 und des Neubau Empfangsgebäudes sollen die daran angrenzenden Bereiche (Durchgangshalle sowie Nord- und Südbau) abgebrochen werden. Die Abbruchmaßnahmen umfassen die oberirdischen Teile der beschriebenen Gebäudeteile wie auch die bestehenden Untergeschosse und somit die kompletten Bauwerke, inkl. aller Medien / Versorgungsanlagen. Weiterhin werden in den jeweiligen Abbruchphasen die öffentlichen Wege vom Baufeld abgetrennt. Die notwendige bauliche Abtrennung des Querbahnsteigs vom Baufeld ist zu realisieren.

title: France – Technical control services – PRESTATIONS DE CONTROLES PERIODIQUES ET PONCTUELS DES EQUIPEMENTS DE LA REGIE DES TRANSPORTS METROPOLITAINS (4 LOTS)
description: 1/ La consultation est décomposée en quatre lots ci-après énoncés : Lot 1 Contrôles périodiques et ponctuels des appareils de levage et monte-charges non accessibles ; Lot 2 Contrôles périodiques et ponctuels des installations électriques ; Lot 3 : Contrôles périodiques et ponctuels des escaliers mécaniques, ascenseurs et monte-charges accessibles ; Lot 4 : Contrôles périodiques et ponctuels des équipements sous pression. Les prestations à réaliser sont décrites et s'exécutent conformément aux dispositions du CCAP ainsi que du CCTP communs à tous les lots, documents joints en annexe du présent Avis d'appel public à la concurrence (AAPC). Les candidats ont la possibilité de soumissionner à un, plusieurs ou à la totalité des lots. Les offres seront examinées lot par lot. Les candidats ne peuvent présenter des offres variables selon le nombre de lots susceptibles d'être obtenus. Chaque lot donne lieu à la passation d'un marché séparé. 2/ Les présents marchés publics sont passés selon une procédure avec négociation, en application des articles L21243, R21244 et R216121 à R216123 du Code de la commande publique. Chaque accord-cadre est conclu avec un seul opérateur économique et exécuté en partie par l'émission de bons de commande, pour les prestations décrites dans les documents contractuels (dans les conditions fixées aux articles R2162-13 et R2162-14 du Code) et en partie par la conclusion de marchés subséquents pour les besoins dont toutes les stipulations contractuelles ne sont pas fixées dans les documents de l'accord-cadre (conformément aux articles R2162-7, R2162-11 et R2162-12 du Code). En application de l'article R2162-4 du Code, les marchés publics sont conclus sans montant minimum d'engagement et avec un montant maximum d'engagement sur leur durée initiale d'un an, à savoir : Lot 1 : 220 000,00 euros HT ; Lot 2 : 250 000,00 euros HT ; Lot 3 : 70 000,00 euros HT ; Lot 4 : 20 000,00 euros HT. 3/ Il s'agit de marchés publics de services qui se réfèrent au Cahier des Clauses Administratives Générales applicable aux marchés publics de fournitures courantes et de services (CCAG/FCS), approuvé par l'arrêté du 30 mars 2021. 4/ Au stade des candidatures, les documents transmis avec l'Avis d'Appel Public à la Concurrence (AAPC), figurent dans le Règlement de la consultation « Phase candidature », joint en annexe de l'AAPC. 5/ Les candidats doivent obligatoirement transmettre leur candidature (et leur offre en phase ultérieure) de façon dématérialisée via le sitewww.achatpublic.com. 6/ La RTM mettra à disposition le Dossier de Consultation des Entreprises (DCE) complet aux candidats admis à déposer une offre, via le site www.achatpublic.com qui fournira à ces derniers les modalités de téléchargement. Les candidats devront transmettre leur offre obligatoirement de façon dématérialisée via le site Internet achatpublic.com. 7/ En phase ultérieure, chaque candidat a l'obligation de visiter certains lieux dans lesquels il sera amené à intervenir, afin de mieux appréhender les conditions d'exécution des prestations. Les modalités pour effectuer la visite seront précisées dans l'Invitation à Soumissionner (IS), document constitutif du Dossier de Consultation des Entreprises (DCE), qui sera transmis aux candidats admis à déposer une offre.

title: Snow removal, de-icing, and related winter maintenance services
description: U.S. Embassy Bucharest, Romania, requests quotations from qualified contractors to provide snow removal, de-icing, and related winter maintenance services at designated Embassy facilities and residences. The Government intends to establish an IDIQ contract under which services may be ordered as needed during each defined winter-season service window. The Contractor shall provide all personnel, supervision, equipment, tools, fuel, personal protective equipment, transportation, insurance, management, and other resources necessary to perform the services, except materials or equipment expressly identified as Government-furnished in the Statement of Work (SOW). This is a fixed-price contract for snow removal and cleaning services for the U.S. Embassy Bucharest. The Government will pay the Contractor the fixed price per hour for standard services that will be satisfactorily performed.

title: Sierra Leone - Resettlement for Transmission Design (Design Package 1)
description: SPECIFIC PROCUREMENT NOTICE (SPN) Country Sierra Leone Project Name Transmission Backbone Project Procurement Title Resettlement for Transmission Design (Design Package 1) Procurement Ref. Number MCA-SL-26-3015 Type of Procurement (goods, works or services as applicable) Consultancy Services Accountable Entity Millennium Challange Account Sierra Leone Publication Date September 03, 2026 Submission Deadline 14:00PM GMT. November 04, 2026, 1. The United States of America, acting through the Millennium Challenge Corporation (�MCC�), and the Government of the Republic of Sierra Leone (the �Government�) signed a Millennium Challenge Compact on September 27, 2024, valued at four hundred eighty million United States Dollars (USD 480,000,000), with an additional fourteen million two hundred thousand United States Dollars (USD 14,200,000) in counterpart funding from the Government of Sierra Leone. The Compact aims to reduce poverty and promote economic growth in Sierra Leone by strengthening the country�s electricity sector. The Government, acting through MCA-Sierra Leone, intends to use a portion of the MCC grant to finance eligible payments under the contract for which this Request for Offers (�RFO�) is issued. 2. The Compact consists of the following three (3) projects: (i) the Transmission Backbone Project, which aims to expand and reinforce Sierra Leone�s electricity transmission network; (ii) the Distribution and Access Project, which aims to improve the reliability of electricity supply and expand access to electricity in selected communities; and (iii) the Power Sector Reform Project, which aims to improve the financial sustainability, governance, and performance of the electricity sector. Full Compact project descriptions and other details are set forth in the Compact which is available at https://assets.mcc.gov/content/uploads/compact-sierra-leone.pdf 3. MCC requires that all beneficiaries of MCC funding, including the Accountable Entity and any applicants, bidders, suppliers, contractors, consultants, sub-consultants, and subcontractors under MCC-funded contracts, observe the highest standards of ethics during the procurement and execution of such contracts. MCC�s Policy on Preventing, Detecting and Remediating Fraud and Corruption in MCC Operations (�MCC�s AFC Policy�) is applicable to all procurements and contracts involving MCC funding and is available on MCC�s website at: https://www.mcc.gov/resources/doc/policy-fraud-and-corruption 4. This RFO follows the General Procurement Notice published in dgMarket on June 4, 2026 and June 16, 2026. 5. MCA-Sierra Leone now invites Offers from legally constituted consulting firms and other eligible organizations to provide Consultant Services for Resettlement for Transmission Design (Design Package 1) (�Offers�). The assignment comprises a Base Period of Eighteen (18) Months for Project Preparation, and an Option Period of Six (6) months for RAP Implementation. Detailed information on the scope of services is provided in the Terms of Reference in Section V of the RFO. 6. This RFO is open to all eligible consulting firms (�Offerors�) that wish to respond. Subject to the restrictions specified in the RFO, Offerors may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications and capacity to carry out the assignment. 7. The Offeror will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method, as defined in the AE Procurement & Policy Guidelines. provided on the MCC website (www.mcc.gov/ppg). The selection process, as described, will include a review and verification of qualifications and past performance, including a reference check, prior to the contract award. 8. Interested Offerors must register their interest by completing the online registration form hosted on Microsoft Forms at the link below. Upon successful registration, Offerors will receive an email containing the link to download the Request for Offers (RFO) and the related procurement documents. Only registered Offerors will receive access to the RFO and any subsequent communications, clarifications, or addenda. Registration link: MCA-SL-26-3015 - Registration Form � Fill out form 9. Please note that a Pre-Offer Conference will be held at 15:00PM GMT on September 17, 2026, as described in the Data Sheet (�DS�), Section II of the Request for Offers (RFO). The conference will be conducted via Microsoft Teams at: Microsoft Teams meeting Join: https://teams.microsoft.com/meet/360970786427609?p=V8WJg5wWCOP587xcdr Meeting ID: 360 970 786 427 609 Passcode: Jw94ZF2n Attendance by all interested Offerors or their representatives is strongly encouraged, but not mandatory. 10. The deadline for submission of Offers is: 14:00PM GMT. November 04, 2026, 11. Only electronic Offers submitted in accordance with the instructions set out in the RFO will be accepted. Late Offers will not be accepted under any circumstances. 12. Contact Information: Attn: Procurement Agent Millennium Challenge Account � -Sierra Leone E-mail: pasierraleone@charleskendall.com with a copy to shiaka.momoh@mca-sl.gov.sl Yours Sincerely, Ndeye Sesay Chief Executive Officer DISCLAIMER: THIS NOTICE IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. FOR MORE INFORMATION ON THIS PROCUREMENT PLEASE CONTRACT THE PERSON NAMED IN THE FULL ANNOUNCEMENT.

title: Germany – Metalworking – 60*.02553 | Los 512 RST Metallgeländer BA1
description: Allgemein: An der Oberkante der Ilmböschung östlich des Stadtschlosses befindet sich ein schmiedeeisernes Geländer, das seit Ende des 19. Jhd. dort existiert. Es besteht aus Rechteckpfosten, Ober- und Untergurt sowie geschwungenen und kreisförmigen Füllungen. Die Pfosten sind auf Travertinsockel/-fundamenten befestigt. Das Geländer soll vor Ort demontiert, in der Werkstatt des AN aufgearbeitet und wieder an der Oberkante der Böschung eingebaut werden. Mehrere Geländerteile fehlen und müssen ersetzt werden. Die Travertinsockel/-fundamente sind möglichst zu erhalten. Sockel/Fundamente, die nicht erhalten werden können, werden neu hergestellt. Der Travertinsockel, inkl. Aussparung wird separat von einem Steinmetz gefertigt, und diesem Gewerk bauseits beigestellt. Das darunterliegende Betonfundament ist im Rahmen diese Gewerks mit herzustellen. Erfahrungen in der Restaurierung und Instandsetzung von historischen Metallbau- und Schmiedearbeiten werden vorausgesetzt. Referenzen über die Restaurierung von denkmalgeschützten Objekten sind zur Angebotsabgabe vorzulegen. Grobmengen: 1 psch Baustelleneinrichtung 95 m Geländer demontieren und aufarbeiten (strahlen, richten, Befestigungen aufarbeiten, feuerverzinken, Farbanstrich) 35 St Fundamente herstellen, Travertinsockel einbauen 57 m saniertes Geländer wieder einbauen 38 m saniertes Geländer zur Einlagerung anliefern

title: Building 13 Stair and Roof Replacement at Castle Point VAMC
description: This notice is for Solicitation Number 36C24227B0002, Project Number 620A4-25-201 Building 13 Stair and Roof Replacement at the VA Hudson Valley Health Care System, Castle Point Campus, 41 Castle Point Road, Wappingers Falls, New York 12590. This shall be a 100% Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) Set-Aside. As a result, all SDVOSBs may submit a bid, which will be considered by the agency. This project is classified under NAICS Code 236220 and has a size standard of $45 Million. The Magnitude of Construction for this project is between $500,000.00 and $1,000,000.00. Scope of Work: The scope of work shall generally consist of, but not limited to the following: The purpose of this project is to for the repair of the exterior architectural features of Building 13 including but not limited to tuckpointing, roof, stair, brick repair/replacement, structural integrity, and elevation repairs. Work includes general construction, alterations, architectural removal and restoration, asbestos remediation, necessary removal of existing structures and construction and certain other items. Contractor shall completely prepare site for building operations, including demolition and removal of existing structures, and furnish labor and materials and perform work for repair of Building 13 required by drawings and specifications. Construction contractors selected by award to perform work at VISN 2 VA facilities, are required to utilize VISN 2 Autodesk Build Construction management platform, also called Autodesk Construction Cloud (ACC). Access to the platform and training portal will be provided by VISN 2 through project Contracting Officer Representative (COR) at no cost for the duration of the project. Autodesk Build is the management and collaborative environment that VISN 2 uses for all its Non-Recurring Maintenance (NRM), Minor Program projects, Feasibility Studies, Commissioning and Retro-Commissioning contracts. There is no user, license, or subscription fee to the contractor for using this cloud-based platform. The Medical Center must maintain its operation 24 hours a day 7 days a week. Therefore, any interruption in service must be scheduled and coordinated with the COR to ensure that no lapses in operation occur. It is the CONTRACTOR'S responsibility to develop a work plan and schedule detailing, at a minimum, the procedures to be employed, Infection Control Risk Assessment (ICRA), the equipment and materials to be used, the interim life safety measure to be used during the work, and a schedule defining the duration of the work with milestone subtasks. NOTICE FOR FILING AGENCY PROTESTS United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Ombudsman Program The USDA is committed to issuing solicitations and awarding contracts in a fair and prompt manner. The Ombudsman Program for Agency Protests (OPAP) was established to address protest issues within the agency, providing an alternative to costly and time-consuming litigation. Operating independently, OPAP offers relief comparable to that granted by the Government Accountability Office (GAO). Interested parties are encouraged to resolve concerns through USDA�s internal Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) process before pursuing external forums such as the GAO. Concerns may be addressed informally or through a formal agency protest filed with either the Contracting Officer or the Ombudsman. Informal Forum with the Ombudsman 1.Initial Point of Contact: Interested parties who believe a specific USDA procurement isunfair or otherwise defective should first direct their concerns to the applicable Contracting Officer. 2.Escalation: If the Contracting Officer is unable to address their concerns, interested partiesare encouraged to contact the USDA Ombudsman for Agency Protests. Under this informalprocess, the agency is not required to suspend contract award performance. Utilization ofthe informal forum does not suspend any time requirement for filing a formal protest withthe agency or other forums. 3.Required Information: To ensure a timely response, interested parties should provide thefollowing information to the Ombudsman: solicitation/contract number, contracting office,Contracting Officer, and solicitation closing date (if applicable). Formal Agency Protest with the Ombudsman 1.Effort to Resolve: Prior to submitting a formal agency protest, protesters must first usetheir best efforts to resolve their concerns with the Contracting Officer through open andfrank discussions. 2.Independent Review: If the protester�s concerns remain unresolved, an IndependentReview is available by the Ombudsman. The protester may file a formal agency protest witheither the Contracting Officer or, alternatively, with the Ombudsman under the OPAP program. Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest periodunless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined in writing to be inthe best interest of the Government. 3.Resolution Timeline: The agency�s goal is to resolve protests within 35 calendar days fromthe date of filing. 4. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104(a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. 5. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. 6. Submission: Formal protests under the OPAP program should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Election of Forum. By initiating a protest with the USDA, the protester agrees not to pursue the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If a protest is filed externally, the agency protest will be dismissed.

title: P233 AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL TOWER AND FLIGHT SIMULATOR FACILITY AT KEESLER AIR FORCE BASE, BILOXI, MS
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT, A MARKET SURVEY FOR WRITTEN INFORMATION ONLY TO IDENTIFY POTENTIAL OFFERORS FOR A DESIGN-BID-BUILD CONSTRUCTION PROJECT TO CONSTRUCT A NEW AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL TOWER AND FLIGHT SIMULATOR FACILITY AT KEESLER AIR FORCE BASE, BILOXI, MS. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS OR AN INVITATION FOR BID. NO CONTRACT WILL BE AWARDED FROM THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO REIMBURSEMENT WILL BE MADE FOR ANY COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH PROVIDING INFORMATION IN RESPONSE TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT OR ANY FOLLOW-UP INFORMATION REQUESTS. No telephone calls will be accepted requesting a bid package or solicitation. There is no bid package or solicitation currently available. In order to protect the procurement integrity of any future procurement that may arise from this announcement, information regarding the technical point of contact will not be given and no appointments for presentations will be made. The anticipated solicitation number is N6945027R0008. The purpose of this notice is for the Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command Southeast (NAVFAC SE) to gain knowledge of qualified and interested parties in any of the following categories: small business, U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) certified 8(a), SBA certified HUBZone, woman-owned small business (WOSB), veteran-owned small business (VOSB), and service disabled veteran-owned small business (SDVOSB). Potential sources should have current relevant qualifications, experience, personnel, and capability to perform this proposed project. The type of solicitation to be issued will depend upon responses to this sources sought notice. The Government will use the sources sought responses along with other market research to make various determinations regarding the procurement. Project Description: This project will construct a new Air Traffic Control Tower (3,983 SF) with Flight Simulator Facility (9,709 SF) adjacent to Base Operations. The facility will be constructed of drilled piling foundation, reinforced concrete wall panels, reinforced concrete floor slabs, and structural steel framing. The facility will include an elevator and a 500 KW backup generator. The construction must comply with Miami-Dade Hurricane codes. This project will comply with Department of Defense Antiterrorism/Force Protection requirements per Unified Facilities Criteria 4-010-01 and Unified Facilities Criteria 3-600-01, Fire protection. A new perimeter fence will need to be install around the new facility. The project includes all utilities, site improvements, pavements, and all necessary work for a complete and usable facilities. The anticipated performance period for base and options on this contract will be 1219 calendar days. The magnitude of construction is between $20,000,000 and $50,000,000. Under the FAR guidelines, the prime contractor must have the capability to perform at least 15 percent of the contract work with its own employees. The anticipated award date is third Quarter FY 27. Interested sources are invited to respond to this Sources Sought announcement. Capability Statements consisting of appropriate documentation will be accepted providing it contains ALL the information required below (items 1-6). Complete submission package shall not exceed 4 pages. The information which must be contained in your response is as follows: 1) Contractor Information: Name and address of company, point of contact with phone number and email address. 2) Type of Business: Identify the company�s business size and socio-economic status (HUBZone, 8(a), SDVOSB, WOSB, etc.) for NAICS Code 236220 applicable to this sources sought. If your firm is claiming HUBZone or 8(a) status, provide a copy of your SBA certification. 3) Bond Capacity: Information must include surety�s name, point of contact, telephone number, email address, and the bonding capacity of at least $50 Million per project, and the maximum aggregate bonding. 4) System for Award Management (SAM): Evidence of registration in the SAM, including Cage Code and Entity Identifier (formerly DUNS Number). 5) Interest: Indicate if a solicitation is issued will your firm/company be submitting a proposal: _____ Yes ______No. 6) Experience Submission Requirements: Responders shall provide a minimum of two (2) to a maximum of five (5) projects including contract numbers, project titles, dollar amounts, project completion dates, performance ratings, and evidence of specific capabilities listed below: Demonstrate Prime Contractor experience constructing vertical construction on an active airfield using a crane that was self-performed; must have a value of approximately $20,000,000 or greater; and were similar in size, scope and complexity to the proposed project. Projects submitted for the Offeror shall be completed within the past seven (7) years of the date of issuance of this announcement. Provide a brief description including completion date and final contract value. If they are not approximately equal to the requested dollar value, identify the dollar value and explain in no more than one paragraph why we should consider the project. The response to this sources sought is not expected to be a proposal, but rather short statements regarding the company�s ability to demonstrate existing-or-developed expertise and experience in relation to the areas specified herein. Submission of Capabilities statement is not a prerequisite to any potential future offerings, but participation will assist the Government in tailoring requirements to be consistent with industry capabilities. After completing its analysis, the Government will determine whether to limit competition among 8(a), HubZone, SDVOSB, VOSB, WOSB, and/or Small Business firms or to proceed with issuing an unrestricted solicitation, inviting full and open competition. Please respond to this announcement no later than 3 NOV 2026, 2:00 PM Eastern Time via email to meaghan.m.pabon.civ@us.navy.mil and aimee.n.johnson2.civ@us.navy.mil. The subject line of the email shall state: P233 KEESLER AFB, AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL TOWER. Emails shall be no more than 5 MB in size. Responses that do not meet all requirements or are not submitted within the allotted time will not be considered. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation.

description: **** Amendment **** Confidentiality: No proprietary, classified, confidential, or sensitive information should be included in your response. The Government reserves the right to use any non-proprietary technical information in any resultant solicitation(s). Protection of Privileged or Confidential Commercial or Financial Information: The Freedom of Information Act (FOIA), 5 U.S.C. � 552, provides individuals with a right to access certain records in the possession of the Federal government, subject to certain exemptions. Exemption 4 of the FOIA permits information to be withheld that is in the nature of "trade secrets and commercial or financial information obtained from a person and privileged or confidential." The term "person" refers to a wide range of entities, including corporations, banks, state governments, agencies of foreign governments, and Native American tribes or nations, who provide information to the government. Information that does not qualify withholding under the Exemption will be disclosed. CMS may invoke Executive Order 12600 in accordance with FOIA Regulation 45 C.F.R. � 5.42. Information provided by entities to CMS in response to this notice may be subject to FOIA disclosure requirements unless protected under Exemption 4 of the Freedom of Information Act. Should entities wish to protect any trade secret or confidential information under Exemption 4, they should mark their submission accordingly citing applicable redactions and non-disclosure rationale. Pre-disclosure redactions and non-disclosure rationale shall be sent via e-mail to the requesting contracting officer with a copy to the CMS FOIA Office at 12600@cms.hhs.gov. If an entity�s submission is not marked and CMS receives a FOIA request related to this notice, the CMS Contracting Officer will notify the entity. The entity will have 10 working days to object to the release of any part of their information submitted to CMS citing relevant case law. Final determination on the applicability of Exemption 4 of the FOIA are made on a case-by-case basis by CMS. The statutory language of the FOIA is codified at 5 U.S.C. � 552(b). Additional information and resources, including the 9 FOIA Exemptions and HHS FOIA Regulation, and examples, can be found on the HHS FOIA Website. **** End of Amendment **** 1. Overview 1.1 Introduction The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) works diligently to crush fraud in federal health care programs, including Medicare and Medicaid. A cornerstone of CMS� program integrity (PI) strategy is focused on using advanced analytics and other investigative techniques to identify potentially problematic actors and stopping them in their tracks. title: Request for Information (RFI) - Drinking Water
description: FEDERAL EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT AGENCY (FEMA) REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) 10/15/2026 The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), Logistics Management Division, Distribution Management Division, Supply Chain Integration Branch, seeks to identify and assess industry capabilities to provide disaster Water in support of emergency response and steady-state operations within the Continental United States (CONUS) and Outside the Continental United States (OCONUS). The information collected will be used to support contingency planning, requirements development, and operational readiness assessments during natural disasters, humanitarian assistance, and other emergency response scenarios. This RFI is issued solely for information gathering purposes to identify sources that can provide support for the Supply Chain Integration Branch. In accordance with FAR 15.101(e), RFIs may be used when the Government wants to obtain price, delivery, other market information, and capabilities for planning purposes. title: Enterprise Electronic Security Systems (ESS) � Nationwide Operations, Maintenance, Integration, and Lifecycle Support
description: The Contractor shall provide comprehensive, enterprise-wide lifecycle support for Electronic Security Systems (ESS) at Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) facilities nationwide. This includes the engineering, design, installation, integration, and commissioning of new systems; preventive and corrective maintenance; inspection, testing, and repair; system modernization and upgrades; system administration and configuration management; software and license support; and 24-hour emergency response. Covered systems include Physical Access Control Systems (PACS), Video Surveillance/Video Management Systems (VSS/VMS), Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS), duress alarms, intercoms, turnstiles, gate arms, elevator-control interfaces, and the associated network infrastructure supporting these systems � primarily built on the Lenel OnGuard and Milestone XProtect platforms. Services span routine, recurring operations and maintenance (priced firm-fixed-price) as well as supplemental, non-routine work such as installations, major component replacement, and modernization projects (priced firm-fixed-price or, when properly justified, time-and-materials). The Contractor is also responsible for staffing key personnel (Program Manager, Project Manager, System Administrator, System Engineer, Lead Technician, and supporting technicians), maintaining a nationwide dispatch/service desk, managing spare parts inventory, supporting cybersecurity and FedRAMP/FISMA compliance for any cloud-based components, and ensuring all work complies with federal physical security, IT security, and records-management requirements � all in support of approximately 35 active facilities at award, with the capacity to scale to roughly 699 facilities nationwide through funded task orders over a 12-month base period plus four option years. The place of performance is nationwide, across Department of Health and Human Services (HHS)-owned, leased, or operated facilities. Specifically: At award: Approximately 35 active facilities, including major National Capital Region (NCR) locations and facilities within all 10 HHS Regions/Hubs. title: Enterprise Electronic Security Systems (ESS) � Nationwide Operations, Maintenance, Integration, and Lifecycle Support
description: The Contractor shall provide comprehensive, enterprise-wide lifecycle support for Electronic Security Systems (ESS) at Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) facilities nationwide. This includes the engineering, design, installation, integration, and commissioning of new systems; preventive and corrective maintenance; inspection, testing, and repair; system modernization and upgrades; system administration and configuration management; software and license support; and 24-hour emergency response. Covered systems include Physical Access Control Systems (PACS), Video Surveillance/Video Management Systems (VSS/VMS), Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS), duress alarms, intercoms, turnstiles, gate arms, elevator-control interfaces, and the associated network infrastructure supporting these systems � primarily built on the Lenel OnGuard and Milestone XProtect platforms. Services span routine, recurring operations and maintenance (priced firm-fixed-price) as well as supplemental, non-routine work such as installations, major component replacement, and modernization projects (priced firm-fixed-price or, when properly justified, time-and-materials). The Contractor is also responsible for staffing key personnel (Program Manager, Project Manager, System Administrator, System Engineer, Lead Technician, and supporting technicians), maintaining a nationwide dispatch/service desk, managing spare parts inventory, supporting cybersecurity and FedRAMP/FISMA compliance for any cloud-based components, and ensuring all work complies with federal physical security, IT security, and records-management requirements � all in support of approximately 35 active facilities at award, with the capacity to scale to roughly 699 facilities nationwide through funded task orders over a 12-month base period plus four option years. The place of performance is nationwide, across Department of Health and Human Services (HHS)-owned, leased, or operated facilities. Specifically: At award: Approximately 35 active facilities, including major National Capital Region (NCR) locations and facilities within all 10 HHS Regions/Hubs. Potential ordering universe: Approximately 699 HHS facilities nationwide, which the contract may expand to through funded task orders (identification in this universe doesn't create an obligation � only facilities in the awarded schedule or a funded task order are actual performance locations

title: IDIQ For Architect Engineer (A/E) Services for Central Office
description: THIS IS A SYNOPSIS OF PROPOSED CONTRACT ACTION. FOLLOW THE INSTRUCTIONS CONTAINED IN THIS NOTICE FOR RESPONDING TO THIS OPPORTUNITY. The Federal Bureau of Prisons (FBOP), Central (CO), anticipates the need for indefinitedelivery indefinite-quantity (IDIQ), firm fixed-price contracts for supplemental architect-engineer (A-E) services, with a one (1) year base requirement and up to four (4) unilaterally exercised option years, with a possibility for a six-month extention as well. The Government is not obligated to exercise any of the option periods. While the Government anticipates multiple awards, no more than four (4) awards are expected. The services will be for various FBOP facilities throughout the United States. See the Statement of Work attachment for description of services. Most projects will take place in a fully occupied, fully operational, secure correctional environment. Most projects require complex design effort and detail along with extensive coordination between design disciplines, the institutions, and Central Office during design and construction. Firms are to perform services as required by the issuance of individual task orders. The guaranteed annual minimum amount of each contract is $10,000.00 and the estimated annual maximum is $10,000,000. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code applicable to this requirement is 541310 (Architectural Services). Interested firms must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) at https://SAM.gov. This requirement will be fulfilled pursuant to the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 36.6 and the Brooks Act. Pursuant to FAR Deviation 36.201(b), for any firm(s) receiving award under this requirement, no construction contract may be awarded to the firm (including any of its subsidiaries or affiliates) that designs the corresponding project Firms having the capabilities to perform the services described in this announcement are invited to respond by submitting Parts I and II of the Standard Form 330 (Architect Engineer Qualifications) dated not more than 12 months before the date of this synopsis. The current version of the form along with any extra pages/sections may be retrieved from www.gsa.gov/forms (Type in "SF330" in the Form Name or Number block for a full listing of the associated forms. *** Include a cover letter detailing your firms name and main office address (as registered in sam.gov), UEI#, Tax ID# (TIN), CAGE code, and main point of contact for your firm through out the solicitation process (phone and e-mail). Submissions should be on standard 8.5'' x 11" format. No extraneous attachments. Selection criteria will be based on the following evaluation factors in descending order of importance: Specialized Experience and Technical Competence (32%) Capacity to Accomplish the Work in the Required Time (demonstrated ability to complete projects on time) (27%) Acceptability of an Established Team of Key Personnel (23%) Professional Qualifications Necessary for Satisfactory Performance (including licensed engineers and architects licensed Nationwide)(18%) Submit details (maximum of one page per project) of not more than five significant and/or complex renovation projects completed in the past five years (Utilize Section F of the SF-330). Identify the lead designer and address the design approach with salient features for each project. Discuss how the client's program, function, image, mission, economic, schedule and operational objectives were satisfied by the overall design/planning solution. Include tangible evidence where possible such as certificates, awards, peer recognition, etc., demonstrating design excellence. Provide a client reference contact for each project, including name, title, address, phone, fax, and email. Submit resumes of key personnel outlining commitment to projects and qualifications and relevant experience as individuals and as a team. Highlight sustainability features incorporated into the project design (e.g., energy/water efficiency, waste reduction, use of recycled materials). Submit a narrative outline of not more than one page describing the firm's project management planning, coordination, scheduling and production facilities, capabilities, and techniques for both design and construction inspection (Utilize Section H of the SF-330). Submit a narrative outline (maximum one page) with examples describing the firm's ability to evaluate/develop accurate preliminary project budgets, ability to control project costs during design process, ability to design within funding limitations, methods used to coordinate construction documents, work of various engineering disciplines, and provide general production quality control (Utilize Section H of the SF-330). No fax or paper submissions. Submit electronically through the JEFS APP BOX at link below: https://jefs.app.box.com/f/336fbbe977394048827a238f901db3a3 All submissions should be in Adobe format. Title the file in the following format: 15BBNF26R70000006_ Company Name_SF330 Architect Engineer (A/E) Services for Central Office Electronic copies of each submission shall be compatible with the following software products: Adobe Acrobat Reader 11 and Microsoft Office Suite 2016. Narrative portions of the submission shall be in Adobe Acrobat portable document file (pdf) searchable text format. The Submitter shall not embed sound or video (e.g., MPEG) files into the submission files. Electronic files shall be clearly identified for each volume, section, and item. The Submitter must ensure electronic files are virus-free and shall run an anti-virus scan before submission. Submissions by mail or hand carried will not be evaluated. All responses must be received no later than Wednesday, November 4, 2026, 10:00 AM MST. It is the responsibility of the Submitter to confirm receipt by contacting Alex Jackson, Contracting Officer, at a4jackson@bop.gov. Failure to submit all required information may result in rejection. All submissions received after the exact time specified for receipt shall be treated as late submissions and will not be considered except under facts and circumstances allowed by the Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR). Based on these submissions, a short-list of no more than six (6) firms will be selected for an interview. Firms should be prepared to discuss their submittals and to demonstrate their ability to fulfill the contract requirements. Final selection will be based on SF-330 submissions and interviews. After the SF-330 review and interview process, four (4) selected firms will be invited to submit a formal proposal and must be prepared to negotiate overhead, profit, and hourly rates for anticipated disciplines for use in negotiating firm-fixed-price contract rates as well as firm-fixed-price task orders to be completed under the contract. All contract awards and task orders thereunder are subject to a determination of fair and reasonable pricing. This acquisition is 100 percent small business set-aside. Firms must be registered in SAM.gov as a small business (see FAR provision 52.219-1 in the Representations & Certifications section of the SAM registration. If you have questions about SAM.gov, Government procurements in general, or need assistance in the preparation of your bid/proposal/offer, a local Procurement Technical Assistance Center (PTAC) may be able to help. The Procurement Technical Assistance Program was authorized by Congress in 1985 in an effort to expand the number of businesses capable of participating in the Government marketplace. To locate a PTAC near you, go to http://www.aptac-us.org.

description: Attachment 1: Combined Synopsis-Solicitation for Commercial Products and Commercial Services Description This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products and commercial services prepared in accordance with the format Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) subpart 12.202, Streamlined Procedures for Evaluation and Solicitation for Commercial Products and Commercial Services, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. The Louis Stokes VA Medical Center in Cleveland, OH, is seeking a qualified contractor to provide all labor, materials, transportation, and supervision for the annual inspection and testing of 18 Cookson Firefly release devices and drop doors. These fail-safe devices are critical for maintaining fire wall integrity; they hold doors open during normal operations and release corrugated fire doors immediately upon fire alarm activation. There is no solicitation available at this time. 2.0 SCOPE OF WORK The Veterans Health Administration (VHA) Non-Expendable Equipment National Program has identified the Environmental Disinfection Systems Pulsed Xenon UV Light as a candidate for a VA-wide (otherwise referred to as national ) contract. Systems that use ultraviolet (UV) light designed to kill, remove, or render inert pathogenic microorganisms present in a closed environment and on hard inanimate surfaces and objects located in that environment (frequently limited to one room). These systems are intended to remove microorganisms from the environment (i.e., most viruses and bacteria, including mycobacteria) and other microbial forms, including spores when using appropriate wavelengths in the UV spectrum. The UV radiation is obtained from dedicated (e.g., low-pressure mercury, pulsed-xenon) lamps that emit radiation in the UV-B and C ranges (e.g., from 200 to 320 nm wavelength); a fixed wavelength of 254 nm is frequently used. The systems are usually automated and include computerized and remote monitoring capabilities. Some systems permit choosing one of several working cycles according to the room disinfection needs. UV environmental disinfection systems are intended for short-term use (e.g., from several minutes to a few hours) in patient rooms, operating rooms, and other healthcare facility closed areas; they are usually used after a terminal cleaning that is performed when a patient is transferred or discharged from a room. The following Minimum Technical Requirements (MTRs) are being considered: FDA Authorized Whole Room Microbial Reduction Devices The contractor shall provide FDA authorized whole room ultraviolet microbial reduction systems. System Architecture Characteristics System shall utilize a high intensity pulsed xenon emitter capable of producing broad spectrum germicidal ultraviolet energy within the 240 315 nm range. System shall operate as a single integrated unit capable of delivering 360-degree germicidal exposure in typical clinical environments. Workflow Characteristics System shall be deployable by a single trained operator. System shall not require staff to reenter the treatment area while cycles are active. System shall support treatment of primary patient care areas as well as adjacent spaces such as restrooms or anterooms through configurable cycle options. Vendor shall provide operator training covering device setup, operation, safety, maintenance, certification, and competency. Technology / Connectivity Characteristics System shall provide a unified operator interface capable of initiating, monitoring, and completing treatment cycles through a single control platform. System shall support cloud-based reporting of cycle completion, operator usage, and device performance analytics. Cloud connectivity features shall function independently of internal facility networks, avoiding reliance on local security credentials or firewalls. Physical / Deployment Characteristics System shall consist of a single mobile unit that can be transported between rooms by one operator. System shall include integrated power management and charging capabilities suitable for frequent deployment within clinical workflows. System shall include durable wheels, handles, and stabilization features appropriate for movement throughout healthcare facilities. System shall be designed for operation in unoccupied clinical rooms, including patient care areas, operating rooms, procedural suites, and utility spaces. For each product identified in the response (brand name and part number), the response must include descriptive literature demonstrating that the product meets or exceeds the MTRs specified above. title: AJ12--Development/Production - Kidney GEC-Specific AAV Vector
description: The following is a Sources Sought/Request for Information notice. This posted notice is not a Pre- Solicitation or Solicitation document. The government is not currently soliciting bids, quotes or proposals at this time; however, reserves the right to do so at a later date. The Harry S Truman Memorial Veterans Hospital, Columbia, MO 65201 has a brand name only requirement for Development/Production- Kidney GEC- Specific AAV Vector. Statement of Work (SOW) For GEC Targeted Adeno Associated Virus Vector Development Contract Description: Development and production of a kidney glomerular endothelial cell specific AAV vector for VA preclinical research. 1.0 Scope of Work: 1.1 This requirement is a VA ORD Merit funded project (#1I21RD001234-01) to develop a kidney glomerular endothelial cell specific viral vector. 1.2 The goal of the project is to build a homing peptide enabled vector platform capable of targeting the glomerular endothelium to treat kidney injury and disease and to enhance traditional pharmacologic approaches. 1.3 The work will modify the capsid of an endothelial specific, non immunogenic viral vector by incorporating a peptide that specifically targets kidney glomerular endothelial cells (GEC), with the objective of increasing specificity, reducing off target transduction, and overcoming known limitations in vector targeting to the kidney. 2.0 Background: 2.1 This requirement in response to RD-01-PILT: ISRM Pilot Project Award I21 was selected for funding by ORD; Merit funded project (1I21RD001234-01). 2.2 Despite aggressive management of blood pressure and glycemic control, the prevalence of kidney disease continues to rise, highlighting the need for adjunctive, individualized approaches that advance precision medicine. The project aims to build a homing peptide enabled vector platform targeting the glomerular endothelium to treat kidney injury and disease and to augment current therapeutic strategies. 2.3 Effective vector targeting of the kidney is impeded by the filtering function of the glomerulus and the risk of off target transduction, which may cause adverse effects. These challenges are compounded by the complex architecture of the kidney. Phage enabled peptide homing provides a powerful tool to refine tissue and cell specificity. Developing a targeted vector for GECs cells central to kidney disease development has strong potential to increase selectivity and minimize off target effects. 2.4 To address this need, the requirement leverages two technologies: (1) Biopanning with phage display to select peptides that specifically target kidney glomerular endothelial cells, and (2) capsid modification of an endothelial specific, non immunogenic vector to improve specificity and reduce off target transduction. 2.5 The services required will: 2.5.1 Validate a GEC targeting peptide and incorporate it into an endothelial specific adeno associated virus (AAV) capsid to control transduction specificity. 2.5.1.1Aim 1 refines phage display selection between murine and human renal versus extra renal endothelial cells to confirm GEC selectivity, followed by incorporation into the AAV capsid 2.5.2 Test the feasibility of the GEC specific AAV vector in culture studies (binding and internalization) and in vivo (biodistribution and transduction efficacy). 2.5.1.2 Aim 2 evaluates the targeting peptide modified AAV vector in murine kidney slices and in vivo biodistribution studies, followed by ex vivo immunofluorescent validation. The vector will also be tested in a murine model of endothelial glomerular filtration barrier injury. 2.6 This requirement will overcome current limitations in kidney specific vector targeting caused by the organ s complex cellular architecture and will create a clinically translatable cell specific vector platform designed to reduce off target effects. 3.0 Technical Requirements/Tasks: 3.1 Within one year of the start date of the funding award. The contractor shall independently perform all technical tasks required to engineer, produce, and validate a kidney glomerular endothelial cell (GEC) specific viral vector. Task one will require a high level of demonstrated proficiency and efficiency to be able to complete within one year. 3.1.1 Task 1: Peptide Incorporation Into Viral Capsid 3.1.1.1 Identified targeting peptides shall be engineered by the contractor into the AAV VP1 capsid at amino acid position 588/589, a well tolerated insertion site. 3.1.1.2 Modified AAV viruses will be produced serially. 3.1.1.3 Verified GEC peptide+AAV capsid plasmids will be used to generate vectors containing an eGFP reporter for quantitative assessment of vector function. 3.1.1.4 Specificity and transduction efficiency will be evaluated across a panel of cell types using flow cytometry. 3.1.1.5 Peptide robustness will be evaluated through iterative comparisons of peptide alone versus peptide displayed on the AAV6 capsid. 3.1.1.6 Fluorescent peptide binding to a biomarker unique to GEC will be quantified (KD, IC50) to confirm specificity. 3.1.1.7 Task one will be considered complete when peptide sequencing is completed in accordance with the research protocol. Receipt of the data readout and a satisfactory progress report that outlines the data and any needed adaptations for the next tasks by end of funding period one will complete the task 3.1.2 Task 2: Will begin once there is satisfactory completion of task one. Testing of GEC Specific Peptide Vector Binding will be performed independently by the contractor beginning at the start of the second funding period and must be complete by the end of the second year of the award 3.1.2.1 Supernatant containing the GEC peptide+vector will be incubated with cultured murine kidney tissue slices to assess binding and internalization. 3.1.2.2 Round 1 panning will use laser capture microdissection to collect GEC bound phage. 3.1.2.3 Rounds 2 and 3 will refine targeting using mixed kidney derived cell populations and control tissues. 3.1.2.4 Uptake in non target cells (e.g., hepatocytes, AEC, RECs) will be collected for analysis of non specific binding. 3.1.2.5 Task two will be considered complete when the results of the testing of the GEC-Specific Peptide Vector Binding are submitted to the research team for review and analysis and deemed acceptable. If revision work is needed that will occur in conjunction with Task 3. Completion of this task will require satisfactory progress report that outlines the data and any needed adaptation for the next task. 3.1.3 Task 3: Specificity and Efficiency Testing of the Modified Vector 3.1.3.1 Bioluminescence imaging will be performed over a time course using luciferase reporter constructs to quantify transduction efficiency and determine optimal timepoints. 3.1.3.2 Renal artery infusion of the GEC peptide modified AAV (or control AAV) will be performed to assess target and off target accumulation. 3.1.3.3 Ex vivo whole organ imaging (IVIS Spectrum) and immunohistochemistry/immunofluorescence will confirm organ and cellular level distribution. 3.1.3.4 Vector genome presence will be assessed by AAV ITR specific PCR. 3.1.3.5 Tissue and plasma samples will be collected to evaluate kidney function and possible off target effects. 3.1.3.6 Task three will be considered complete when the research team and facility have determined the data report from the efficiency testing are acceptable and a final report outlining all data, interpretations of the data and conclusions and by the end of the second year of the award. 3.1.3.7 Reported data will be generated and sent to the Primary Investigator by the end of each funding period as outlined in the tasks above. 3.2 Other requirements 3.2.1 Quarterly reporting 3.2.1.1 From date of award onward the awardee shall provide quarterly reports verifying what tasks were completed, current stage and any recent or pending results in alignment with the three tasks 3.1.1, 3.1.2, and 3.1.3 from the VA ORD Merit funded project (#1I21RD001234-

title: Earned Wage Access
description: Request for Information # 70T01027I7663N001 Earned Wage Access Services 1. Purpose The Transportation Security Administration (TSA) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to conduct market research on commercially available Earned Wage Access (EWA) services and to identify capable vendors that may be able to provide a secure, fully managed EWA solution for eligible TSA employees. Information received will support acquisition planning, help TSA assess industry capabilities and implementation approaches, and inform the development of any future solicitation. This RFI is for planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation or commitment by the Government. 2. Anticipated Scope TSA anticipates seeking a Contractor to provide, operate, maintain, and support a voluntary EWA platform for eligible TSA employees. The anticipated service includes secure integration with TSA�s designated Federal payroll provider, employee enrollment and identity verification, earned-wage balance calculation, employee fund-transfer options, customer support, platform maintenance, security and compliance reporting, and program management. The attached draft Performance Work Statement provides additional detail regarding the anticipated scope and requirements. 3. Background TSA employs a geographically dispersed workforce across the United States and U.S. territories. TSA Human Capital is exploring EWA as a potential voluntary employee service to support financial readiness and stability by enabling employees to access a portion of wages they have already earned before the standard biweekly Federal payroll date. The intended service would offer an alternative to high-cost lending products, credit cards, or emergency loans, while preserving the integrity of official Federal payroll processes and avoiding direct costs to the U.S. Government. 4. Period and Place of Performance TSA anticipates that any resulting contract may include a one-year base period with subsequent option periods; however, the final period of performance and contract structure will be determined through acquisition planning. Performance is expected to occur primarily at Contractor facilities and in Contractor-hosted cloud environments, with services supporting TSA employees located throughout all U.S. States and U.S. territories. The Contractor may be required to participate in virtual or in-person meetings with TSA personnel as directed by the Government. 5. Performance Outcomes and Objectives The anticipated EWA service should provide eligible, voluntarily enrolled TSA employees with a secure, reliable, and accessible means to access earned but unpaid wages between regular pay cycles. The Contractor should deliver a highly available platform; protect employee and Government information; provide transparent fee disclosures; maintain employee support services; and ensure the solution does not disrupt, alter, or delay official Federal payroll operations. The Contractor will also be expected to maintain appropriate financial capacity, assume responsibility for EWA transactions, provide meaningful performance reporting, and support service continuity during Federal Government shutdowns. 6. Transition TSA does not currently have an existing contract for EWA services. Therefore, any future Contractor would be responsible for transition-in activities necessary to establish a new EWA capability, including implementation planning, coordination with TSA and the designated payroll provider, secure integration and testing, operational readiness activities, and support for employee launch communications as directed by TSA. The Contractor would also be expected to provide transition-out support at the conclusion of the contract or upon Government direction, including secure transfer of Government data and records, continuity coordination, knowledge transfer, and disposition or sanitization of Government Furnished Information, as applicable. 7. Performance Constraints The anticipated service must be provided at no direct cost to the U.S. Government and must not interfere with official Federal payroll processing. The Contractor will be expected to meet applicable Federal security, privacy, accessibility, and records-management requirements, including use of a FedRAMP-authorized environment as applicable and conformance with Section 508 requirements for information and communications technology. The Contractor must assume sole financial and legal responsibility for EWA funds and transactions, maintain transparent employee fee disclosures, support employees nationwide and in U.S. territories, and demonstrate the capability to continue EWA operations during a partial or full Federal Government shutdown in accordance with the attached PWS. 8. Responses to the RFI Should Include Cover Letter, One-Page Limit: Interested parties should provide a one-page cover letter that identifies the company�s legal name, business address, Unique Entity Identifier, if available, business size and socioeconomic status, primary point of contact, NAICS codes and applicable Federal contract vehicles. The letter should briefly state the organization�s interest in the requirement and indicate whether the organization anticipates serving as a prime contractor or through a teaming arrangement. Capabilities Statement, Five-Page Limit: Interested parties should submit a capabilities statement describing their ability to meet the anticipated EWA requirement described in the attached PWS. The capabilities statement should summarize the organization�s EWA platform and employee-support capabilities; relevant experience with Federal or similarly regulated payroll-system integrations; FedRAMP, security, privacy, and Section 508 capabilities; financial capacity to fund wage advances; approach to transaction liability and Government-shutdown continuity; comparable past performance; anticipated implementation approach and timeline; and ability to provide performance reporting, transition support, and transparent employee fee disclosures. Respondents may also identify recommended refinements or considerations for TSA�s future acquisition approach. Responses to Government Questions, No Page Limit: In addition to the cover letter and capabilities statement, interested parties should provide concise responses to the following questions. title: IDIQ For Architect Engineer (A/E) Services for Central Office
description: *10/21/2026- Amendment posted of Questions and responses posed by contractors. Submission due date reemains the same. THIS IS A SYNOPSIS OF PROPOSED CONTRACT ACTION. FOLLOW THE INSTRUCTIONS CONTAINED IN THIS NOTICE FOR RESPONDING TO THIS OPPORTUNITY. The Federal Bureau of Prisons (FBOP), Central (CO), anticipates the need for indefinitedelivery indefinite-quantity (IDIQ), firm fixed-price contracts for supplemental architect-engineer (A-E) services, with a one (1) year base requirement and up to four (4) unilaterally exercised option years, with a possibility for a six-month extention as well. The Government is not obligated to exercise any of the option periods. While the Government anticipates multiple awards, no more than four (4) awards are expected. The services will be for various FBOP facilities throughout the United States. See the Statement of Work attachment for description of services. Most projects will take place in a fully occupied, fully operational, secure correctional environment. Most projects require complex design effort and detail along with extensive coordination between design disciplines, the institutions, and Central Office during design and construction. Firms are to perform services as required by the issuance of individual task orders. The guaranteed annual minimum amount of each contract is $10,000.00 and the estimated annual maximum is $10,000,000. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code applicable to this requirement is 541310 (Architectural Services). Interested firms must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) at https://SAM.gov. This requirement will be fulfilled pursuant to the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 36.6 and the Brooks Act. Pursuant to FAR Deviation 36.201(b), for any firm(s) receiving award under this requirement, no construction contract may be awarded to the firm (including any of its subsidiaries or affiliates) that designs the corresponding project Firms having the capabilities to perform the services described in this announcement are invited to respond by submitting Parts I and II of the Standard Form 330 (Architect Engineer Qualifications) dated not more than 12 months before the date of this synopsis. The current version of the form along with any extra pages/sections may be retrieved from www.gsa.gov/forms (Type in "SF330" in the Form Name or Number block for a full listing of the associated forms. *** Include a cover letter detailing your firms name and main office address (as registered in sam.gov), UEI#, Tax ID# (TIN), CAGE code, and main point of contact for your firm through out the solicitation process (phone and e-mail). Submissions should be on standard 8.5'' x 11" format. No extraneous attachments. Selection criteria will be based on the following evaluation factors in descending order of importance: Specialized Experience and Technical Competence (32%) Capacity to Accomplish the Work in the Required Time (demonstrated ability to complete projects on time) (27%) Acceptability of an Established Team of Key Personnel (23%) Professional Qualifications Necessary for Satisfactory Performance (including licensed engineers and architects licensed Nationwide)(18%) Submit details (maximum of one page per project) of not more than five significant and/or complex renovation projects completed in the past five years (Utilize Section F of the SF-330). Identify the lead designer and address the design approach with salient features for each project. Discuss how the client's program, function, image, mission, economic, schedule and operational objectives were satisfied by the overall design/planning solution. Include tangible evidence where possible such as certificates, awards, peer recognition, etc., demonstrating design excellence. Provide a client reference contact for each project, including name, title, address, phone, fax, and email. Submit resumes of key personnel outlining commitment to projects and qualifications and relevant experience as individuals and as a team. Highlight sustainability features incorporated into the project design (e.g., energy/water efficiency, waste reduction, use of recycled materials). Submit a narrative outline of not more than one page describing the firm's project management planning, coordination, scheduling and production facilities, capabilities, and techniques for both design and construction inspection (Utilize Section H of the SF-330). Submit a narrative outline (maximum one page) with examples describing the firm's ability to evaluate/develop accurate preliminary project budgets, ability to control project costs during design process, ability to design within funding limitations, methods used to coordinate construction documents, work of various engineering disciplines, and provide general production quality control (Utilize Section H of the SF-330). No fax or paper submissions. Submit electronically through the JEFS APP BOX at link below: https://jefs.app.box.com/f/336fbbe977394048827a238f901db3a3 All submissions should be in Adobe format. Title the file in the following format: 15BBNF26R70000006_ Company Name_SF330 Architect Engineer (A/E) Services for Central Office Electronic copies of each submission shall be compatible with the following software products: Adobe Acrobat Reader 11 and Microsoft Office Suite 2016. Narrative portions of the submission shall be in Adobe Acrobat portable document file (pdf) searchable text format. The Submitter shall not embed sound or video (e.g., MPEG) files into the submission files. Electronic files shall be clearly identified for each volume, section, and item. The Submitter must ensure electronic files are virus-free and shall run an anti-virus scan before submission. Submissions by mail or hand carried will not be evaluated. All responses must be received no later than Wednesday, November 4, 2026, 10:00 AM MST. It is the responsibility of the Submitter to confirm receipt by contacting Alex Jackson, Contracting Officer, at a4jackson@bop.gov. Failure to submit all required information may result in rejection. All submissions received after the exact time specified for receipt shall be treated as late submissions and will not be considered except under facts and circumstances allowed by the Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR). Based on these submissions, a short-list of no more than six (6) firms will be selected for an interview. Firms should be prepared to discuss their submittals and to demonstrate their ability to fulfill the contract requirements. Final selection will be based on SF-330 submissions and interviews. After the SF-330 review and interview process, four (4) selected firms will be invited to submit a formal proposal and must be prepared to negotiate overhead, profit, and hourly rates for anticipated disciplines for use in negotiating firm-fixed-price contract rates as well as firm-fixed-price task orders to be completed under the contract. All contract awards and task orders thereunder are subject to a determination of fair and reasonable pricing. This acquisition is 100 percent small business set-aside. Firms must be registered in SAM.gov as a small business (see FAR provision 52.219-1 in the Representations & Certifications section of the SAM registration. If you have questions about SAM.gov, Government procurements in general, or need assistance in the preparation of your bid/proposal/offer, a local Procurement Technical Assistance Center (PTAC) may be able to help. The Procurement Technical Assistance Program was authorized by Congress in 1985 in an effort to expand the number of businesses capable of participating in the Government marketplace. To locate a PTAC near you, go to http://www.aptac-us.org.

title: Enterprise RFID Technology, Installation, and Azure WIMS Integration
description: United States Census Bureau (USCB) Enterprise RFID Technology, Installation, and Azure WIMS Integration REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) This RFI is solely for information and planning purposes � it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. Further, the USCB is at the early stages of market research and is not, at this time, seeking proposals and will not accept unsolicited proposals. Interested parties are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI; all costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested party�s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future RFP, if any is issued. 1.0 Purpose The U.S. Census Bureau (USCB) issues this Request for Information (RFI) for market research under Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10 to understand current business practices and identify industry capabilities for furnishing, installing, configuring, testing, and integrating radio frequency identification (RFID) technology with the USCB�s existing Warehouse Inventory Management System (WIMS). The USCB seeks industry input on these types of services and expertise in achieving the desired objectives in accordance with federal requirements. To date, the USCB has already developed a scalable WIMS platform using Microsoft technologies in its Microsoft Azure environment. This RFI does not seek a replacement warehouse management platform. The USCB�s primary interest is to acquire industry recommendations on RFID equipment and supporting software, facility deployment and integration services, and secure delivery of RFID event data into the existing WIMS environment. The USCB believes industry has the best knowledge of current offerings and how to plan for, acquire, and integrate evolving technology trends. Vendors are encouraged to provide recommendations and describe innovative, commercially available, and proven approaches that address the objectives detailed within this RFI without being constrained by a prescriptive equipment design or configuration. 2.0 Background and Operational Environment The USCB manages survey forms, printing and mailing materials, shipping supplies, and other inventory supporting demographic, economic, and decennial programs, including preparations for 2030 Census tests. Inventory is received, stored, moved, issued, transferred, and shipped through multiple facilities. Automated identification and transaction capture can reduce manual inventory handling and improve the accuracy and timeliness of enterprise inventory records. Potential locations include National Processing Center operations in Charlestown, Indiana; Census Bureau Headquarters in Suitland, Maryland; a warehouse in Franconia, Virginia; Regional Offices; and other Government-designated facilities. Actual locations, installation scope, sequencing, and site access would be determined by the Government. These locations may have different layouts, physical security restrictions, network conditions, and operating requirements. 3.0 Objectives and Mission-Critical Capability Areas The USCB intends to leverage industry knowledge, feedback, recommendations, and expertise on proven approaches and best practices that achieve the objectives listed below. 3.1 RFID identification and multi-level tracking The USCB is interested in tracking at the item or box, pallet, and rack or storage-location levels. Industry recommendations may include passive or active RFID, hybrid approaches, or complementary identification methods where appropriate. Recommended solutions should support reliable identification and location/movement events during receiving, putaway, internal transfers, picking, shipping, cycle counting, and reconciliation. Input is requested to address read accuracy, interference, duplicate or missed events, and the practical limits of location precision. 3.2 Equipment provision, site assessment, and installation The contemplated effort includes facility assessments; design and equipment selection; provision of tags, readers, antennas, handheld or mobile equipment, portals, and supporting components as appropriate; physical installation and configuration; and operational testing. Respondents shall provide input into the considerations made in regards to site dependencies, secured-space work practices, commissioning, warranties, support, and expansion to additional facilities, as directed. 3.3 Secure integration with existing Microsoft Azure WIMS The RFID solution must exchange usable, timely data with the existing Government WIMS rather than create a competing inventory system of record. Respondents are requested to recommend integration of reader and edge-device feeds with Azure-hosted WIMS through appropriate secure interfaces, APIs, messaging, middleware, or other standards-based methods. Anticipated work may include event filtering, data mapping to Government inventory identifiers and locations, interface development, custom fields or components as needed, error handling, testing, documentation, and knowledge transfer. Specific Azure services and interface specifications will be coordinated with the Government during subsequent planning. 3.4 Security, reliability, and sustainment The USCB seeks recommended approaches and solutions suitable for controlled federal facilities and integration with its existing authorized cloud boundary, subject to applicable security review and approval. Respondents are requested to provide information which describes secure communications, device administration, access control, logging, resilience during network interruptions, patching, lifecycle support, and long-term costs. The USCB seeks recommended approaches which permit Government operation and sustainment without unnecessary vendor lock-in. 4.0 Industry Response and Feedback Questions A. RFID technology and operational performance 1. Describe your recommended technology and architecture for identifying and tracking individual items or boxes, pallets, and racks or storage locations in multiple warehouse facilities. Explain any recommended RFID or hybrid approaches. 2. Identify the major hardware and software components your recommended approach would provide, including tags, fixed or mobile readers, antennas, portals, edge components, and management tools. Distinguish commercial products from custom components. 3. How would your solution capture receiving, putaway, internal movement, picking, shipping, transfers, and cycle-count events, and associate them with the correct inventory identifiers and locations? 4. What read accuracy and location precision can realistically be achieved, and how do you address dense racks, metal, packaging, interference, missed reads, and duplicate events? 5. What mobile, handheld, exception-resolution, and offline or intermittent-connectivity capabilities are available for warehouse operators? B. Facility assessment, installation, and rollout 6. Describe your approach to surveying facilities, developing a site-specific equipment design, and determining reader, antenna, portal, and network placement. 7. Describe your ability to furnish, install, configure, and commission equipment in secured Government spaces at Charlestown, IN; Suitland, MD; Franconia, VA; Regional Offices; and other locations as directed. Identify subcontractor dependencies. 8. What facility, electrical, networking, physical security, access, and Government-furnished resources would typically be needed for installation and operation? 9. Identify a phased pilot-to-enterprise deployment approach, including indicative schedule, testing and acceptance criteria, and the approach for minimizing disruption to ongoing warehouse operations.
