title: US Government Seeks to Lease Office Space around Hanscom AFB
description: 1. DISCLAIMER This is a Request for Information (RFI) / Sources Sought notice only. This notice is issued solely for market research, information, and planning purposes; it does not constitute a Request for Quote (RFQ) or a promise to issue an RFQ in the future. The Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. 2. PURPOSE The United States Air Force is conducting market research to identify potential sources capable of providing leased, off-base commercial office space in a 10-mile radius of Hanscom AFB, MA, 01731 3. MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS To be considered, the proposed space must meet the following minimum parameters: Space Type: Classification Feasibility: Explicitly state what classification levels the space can support today (e.g., Unclassified, Secret/Collateral, TS/SCI, JWICS) and what upgrades would be required to meet higher levels. If no current classification levels exist, is there an ability to add them? Would upgrades remain in place once contract ends? The Government is assessing the full spectrum of security capabilities available in the local market. Please feel free to respond with what you currently have to offer, even if your facility does not meet all preferred security thresholds. For example, if you possess functional Unclassified administrative space and Secret-level secure space, but lack active JWICS (Joint Worldwide Intelligence Communications System) capabilities, we still strongly encourage you to submit a response. The Government is highly interested in reviewing partial, mixed, or upgradeable space configurations to determine how they might support our broader mission requirements. Space Outfitting & Furnishing Status: To assist the Government in assessing transition timelines and potential cost savings, please address the following regarding the proposed space: Existing Inventory: Indicate whether the proposed space is currently unfurnished or contains existing, usable furniture (e.g., modular cubicles, desks, conference tables) that can be utilized to reduce lead times. Installation Capabilities: Specify if the management company offers turnkey installation services for government-furnished or custom-designed cubicles, including any associated fee structures. Capacity: Must accommodate between eighty (80) and one hundred (100) personnel. Square Footage (ABOA): A minimum of 11,200 square feet up to a maximum of approximately 21,000 square feet of American National Standards Institute (ANSI)/ Building Owners and Managers Association (BOMA) Office Area (ABOA). Offers falling within this range that optimize spatial efficiency and allow for potential growth up to the maximum personnel count are highly encouraged Conference and Collaborative Space: Primary Requirement: At least one (1) dedicated conference or collaborative room capable of comfortably seating a minimum of twenty-five (25) personnel. The minimum size for this primary meeting space is 500 square feet. Preferred Option: The availability of secondary conference rooms, huddle spaces, or break-out areas within the offered space is highly desirable to support flexible mission workflows and concurrent meetings. Connectivity: Space must be capable of supporting standard commercial internet/ WiFi service installation. Parking: How many parking spaces are available? Covered garage parking is a �nice to have" Location: Must be located within a 10-mile radius of Hanscom AFB Occupancy and Lease Term The Government is seeking a lease structure consisting of a one-year base period with four consecutive one-year option periods, targeted for occupancy in early 2027. Contract Period | Estimated Duration | Target Timeline / Effective Dates Base Period | 12 Months | April 1, 2027 � March 31, 2028 Option Period 1 | 12 Months | April 1, 2028 � March 31, 2029 Option Period 2 | 12 Months | April 1, 2029 � March 31, 2030 Option Period 3 | 12 Months | April 1, 2030 � March 31, 2031 Option Period 4 | 12 Months | April 1, 2031 � March 31, 2032 Target Occupancy Date: April 1, 2027 (subject to adjustments based on build-out and award timelines). Estimated Cost Range / Rental Rates: Provide an estimated, non-binding rental rate range for the proposed space, expressed as a fully serviced (gross) rate per rentable square foot (RSF) per year. Please specify what utilities, janitorial services, or common area maintenance (CAM) fees are included in this estimated rate, as well as any estimated costs for Tenant Improvements (TI) required to meet the security/furniture requirements. If utilities are not included, please provide an estimated average cost per month for necessary utilities and number of people the estimate is based on 4. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS Interested property owners, brokers, or authorized representatives who can meet the above requirements are requested to submit a brief capability statement. Responses should include the following: Property Information: Address and brief description of the building. Available Space: Exact ABOA square footage available. Floor Plans/Photos: Include photos showing the current layout. Availability: Date the space will be available for occupancy or tenant improvements. Point of Contact: Name, email, and phone number of the property representative. 5. RESPONSE DEADLINE Responses must be submitted via email to Michael Dunford at michael.dunford@us.af.mil and copy AFLCMC.WVG.LookingGlass-Next@us.af.mil no later than 3:00PM on October 28, 2026. Please include the Notice ID in the subject line of your email.

title: NOI - B2B Award entitled - Developing Red Cell-Sp
description: (i)This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordancewith the format in FAR Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information includedin this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; proposals are beingrequested, and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. (ii)The solicitation number is 75N98027Q00017. This solicitation is issued as a Notice ofIntent (NOI) for a non-competitive combined synopsis/solicitation to award a contract orpurchase order without providing for full and open competition (including brand-name, ifapplicable). This acquisition is conducted under the authority of FAR 12.603, Streamlined Solicitation for Commercial Products or Commercial Services, and is not expected to exceed the simplified acquisition threshold. Additional authority includes 41 U.S.C. 1901 and FAR 6.302-3(a)(2)(ii). The National Institutes of Health (NIH), Office of the Director, Office of Acquisitions, intends to negotiate and award a purchase order on a non-competitive basis to Purdue University, Purdue Institute for Drug Discovery (DRUG), 575 Stadium Mall Drive, West Lafayette, IN 47907, for the synthesis, scale-up, and characterization of lead Spleen Tyrosine Kinase (SYK) inhibitors in support of the NIH Bench-to-Bedside study "Developing Red Cell-Specific Spleen Tyrosine Kinase (SYK) Inhibitors for Treating Sickle Cell Disease." Rationale for non-competitive award: The proposed acquisition is a continuation of project-specific medicinal chemistry work under the NIH Bench-to-Bedside study "Developing Red Cell-Specific Spleen Tyrosine Kinase (SYK) Inhibitors for Treating Sickle Cell Disease." Dr. Philip S. Low's laboratory at Purdue University is the identified extramural medicinal chemistry collaborator for this project and has performed the prior design and synthesis work associated with the SYK inhibitor candidates being advanced under the study. The Year 1 requirement is specifically for the synthesis, scale-up, and characterization of lead SYK inhibitors S1115 and S1213 for subsequent biological evaluation by NIH investigators. Purdue possesses the project-specific knowledge and experience associated with these compounds. Use of another source would require duplication of prior research before the source could continue the current effort, resulting in delay and technical risk. Based on these circumstances, Purdue University is the only source reasonably available to perform this specific Year 1 requirement. (iii) The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular 2026-01, effective 03/13/2026. description: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Network Contracting Office (NCO) 2, intends to issue Solicitation 36C24226R0128 for Project 561-26-104 Repair Operating Room (OR) & Bathroom Leaks at the East Orange VA Medical Center, 385 Tremont Ave, East Orange, NJ 07018. This notice is for pre-solicitation purposes only and is issued to provide advance notice of the Government's intent to solicit this construction requirement. This notice is not a request for quotes, proposals, or bids, and no contract award will be made as a result of this announcement. The official solicitation is anticipated to be posted on or about October 19, 2026, on SAM.gov, at which time all solicitation documents, including the Statement of Work, drawings, specifications, and proposal submission instructions, will be made available. This procurement is anticipated to be issued as a 100% Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) set-aside. Eligible SDVOSBs are encouraged to submit an offer upon release of the solicitation. All prospective offerors must be currently registered in www.sam.gov, www.dnb.com (Duns and Bradstreet) and be registered and verified as a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) in https://search.certifications.sba.gov/ at the time of offer submission and before award of this procurement. The applicable NAICS Code is 236220 with a small business size standard of $45.0 million. The Magnitude of Construction for this project is between $100,000 and $250,000. Scope of Work: The work generally consists of renovating a bathroom to correct water intrusion affecting the sterile area below and replacing deteriorated flooring in operating room areas. Work includes demolition; plumbing modifications; installation of wall-hung toilets; wall, floor tile, and associated finish work; approximately 1,600 square feet of resinous flooring with integral cove base; substrate preparation and moisture testing/remediation; associated MEP modifications; infection-control containment; and restoration of affected areas. Work will be performed in an active healthcare environment and will require coordination with VA operations, infection-control measures, and phased/after-hours work as required by the contract documents, all in accordance with the solicitation drawings, specifications, and Statement of Work. Project Completion: 99 Calendar Days from Notice to Proceed (NTP). All other details and information shall be contained in the solicitation which shall be posted on www.sam.gov. The response submittal address, date and time will be included in the solicitation.

The Defense Health Agency has a requirement for non-personal services providing qualified labor and management necessary to perform nutrition care food management, supervisory, technical, administrative, and clerical services that focus primarily on the following areas: dining facility management functions, therapeutic food preparation, patient tray assembly and delivery service, clinical training, facility sanitation, janitorial duties as it relates to the services being provided, and the associated logistics analysis and management functions in support of the Nutrition Care Divisions for five (5) Military Medical Treatment Facilities (MTFs). The following MTFs requiring the Nutrition Care Food Service support are: Weed Army Community Hospital (Fort Irwin, California), General Leonard Wood Community Hospital (Fort Leonard Wood, Missouri), Irwin Army Community Hospital (Fort Riley, Kansas), Winn Army Community Hospital (Fort Stewart, Georgia), and Keller Army Community Hospital (West Point, New York). A transition period of 1 December 2026 � 31 January 2027, base period of 1 February 2027 � 30 September 2027, and two (2) twelve-month option periods through 30 September 2029 are contemplated. The contract will be firm-fixed-price, with a set monthly price established per MTF. Multiple contracts may be awarded, up to one (1) per MTF. The Randolph Sheppard Act (RSA) applies to this requirement; therefore, priority will be given to any responsive State Licensing Agency (SLA) pursuant to the RSA. The priority established by the RSA applies to the award of contracts for the operation of cafeterias on Federal property. NOTE: The evaluation criteria will be the same for all offerors, including any responsible SLA. However, the solicitation will be issued on a full-and-open basis with a small business participation (eg, subcontracting) plan as one of the evaluation criteria for other-than-small businesses and non-SLAs. title: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI): FORT BRAGG, NC (FBNC) FOOD SERVICES SUPPORT
description: DISCLAIMER / SPECIAL NOTICE: This notice is issued solely for information and planning purposes � it does not constitute a Request for Quotation (RFQ), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFQ, IFB, or RFP in the future. This notice does not commit the U.S. Government to contract for any supply or service. Further, the U.S. Government is not seeking quotes, bids, or proposals at this time and will not accept unsolicited proposals in response to this Request for Information. The U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. Submittals will not be returned to the responder. Not responding to this notice does not preclude participation in any future RFQ, IFB, or RFP, if any is issued. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on the Government-wide Point of Entry (GPE). It is the responsibility of potential offerors to monitor the GPE for additional information pertaining to this requirement. The GPE is located at sam.gov. The purpose of this sources sought for is to gather technical, operational, and capability feedback from industry to evaluate a potential requirement for food service support at Fort Bragg, NC. The government is seeking information in the following areas: Vendor Pool Capabilities: The existence and depth of capable prime contractors to execute high-volume installation food services and specialized cook support. Security Compliance Readiness: Industry capacity to comply with stringent physical access control, HSPD-12/Tier 1 background checks, Common Access Card (CAC) issuance procedures, and pre-start SECRET clearance requirements for designated facilities and TDY missions. Operational Feedback: Industry feedback on transition lead times, potential risk factors, and contract structure. Socioeconomic Alignment: Market availability of qualified Small Businesses, 8(a), SDVOSBs, WOSBs, and HUBZone firms to inform set-aside determinations and teaming strategies. See the attached RFI for FBNC FFS Security Clearance document for full details.
